newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil firmer as buyers emerge.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil firmer as buyers emerge.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were firmer at midday on Friday as more buyers emerged following Thursday's physical trades as well as the firm undertone on crude values, brokers said.
"Wall Streeters are bidding up the market," one broker said.
Firmer swaps valus was also put down to trading firms and banks playing the East-West spread by buying the East and selling the West, they said.
July swaps was quoted at $21.00/$21.05 per barrel , while August gained 30 cents at $21.90/$22.00 per barrel.
September also gained 30 cents to be quoted at $22.75/$22.90, with a trade seen at $22.78 per barrel.
Two physical gas oil cargoes totalling 350,000 barrels for early August liftings were traded on Thursday at $20.70 per barrel, up 10 cents from Wednesday's trade.
The drop of 849,000 barrels in Singapore weekly middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 16 to 10.615 million barrels also brought some cheer to the long-suffering gas oil market.
The Singapore Trade Development Board said middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 16 were down 849,000 barrels to 10.615 million barrels.
But traders said 10 million barrels are still high compared to the normal levels of around six to eight million barrels, while China remained absent from the market.

The swaps jet fuel/gas oil regrade remained steady at the $1.80/$2.00 range, but the physical spread continued to widen to more than $3.00 per barrel. Traders attributed this anomaly to physical sellers trying to meet the buying interest from a Singapore trader who has been bidding at firm levels.
Fuel oil swaps rose on the back of intermonth spread trading despite the slightly softer tone on physical market.

August/September spread has widened from the parity values seen oevr the past week, with August indicated at $97.75/$98.75 and September at $98.25/$99.00 from Thursday's $97.75/$98.50 for both months.
